open_obligations: Note that the result is a theoretical protocol, not an observation of obfuscation in practice.
Check that the rho-stability assumption holds for the harder questions Michael et al. have in mind.
Note Michael et al.'s free-text debates are not recursive, unlike the protocol.
in.other_title: Prover-estimator debate mitigates the obfuscated arguments problem in recursive debate
in.rationale: Michael et al. do not observe obfuscated arguments to be a significant problem in their free-text debates with evidence quoting and judge interaction, contrast these with debates scaffolded with explicit recursive structure, and say future work running debates on harder questions can monitor whether obfuscated arguments become an obstacle in practice. Brown-Cohen et al. state that existing recursive debate protocols run into the obfuscated arguments problem and propose prover-estimator debate, which under stability assumptions lets an honest debater win with computational efficiency comparable to its opponent, mitigating obfuscation; the result is theoretical and gives no empirical evidence on whether obfuscation arises in practice.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether obfuscated arguments are an obstacle for debate, for recursive debate protocols under stability assumptions and for free-text debates with evidence quoting and judge interaction

text: The authors report that they do not observe obfuscated arguments to be a significant problem in their setting, noting differences from other debates (explicit recursive structure scaffolding, no grounding in evidence or judge interaction, small-scale experiments on tricky questions). They state that future work running debates on harder questions can monitor whether obfuscated arguments become an obstacle in practice.
title: Will obfuscated arguments become an obstacle for debate on harder questions?
